## Who it's for
Women 30–55 who want a daily peptide step in their skincare routine.

**Audience (`product.json`, the dealer's default):** women only: the image question never asks men or women; the dealer casts women and refuses `--audience men`.

## What it is (bible, one line)
Topical peptide skin support focused on collagen, elastin, firmness, and the skin’s natural repair process.

## Creative direction (bible)
- Beauty and fitness positioning — lean and fit, never bodybuilding.
- Core demo is the 40-year-old mom, same as GLP-1.
- Palette: pinks, tans and beige. No oranges or greens.
- Teach what a peptide skin cream actually does. GHK-Cu is a copper peptide that signals skin to support its own collagen and repair — say it plainly, never assume the viewer knows what “peptide” means.
- Differentiate from ordinary moisturizers and serums: this works at the signal level (collagen, elastin, repair), not just surface hydration. Make the “why it’s different” explicit.
- Pair each benefit with a quick reason-why for context (e.g. “copper peptides support the collagen skin makes less of with age”), not a bare claim.

## Hard stops (this product)
- Lines the screening table marks ❌ / Hard NO conflict: never. Everything that is not a Hard NO is wording, and wording is free.
- **Name:** "GHK PEPTIDE CREAM" on Meta / Google / TikTok; "GHK-CU CREAM" only on H2 (and then no line that says "GHK Peptide
  Cream"). Never "copper", never "-Cu" on its own, never "GHK-Cu" outside that H2 product name.
- Skin support only, "-looking" where the bible says it. No wrinkles, fine lines, sagging, spots, acne, scars or any skin condition;
  no "anti-aging", "reverse", "erase", "years younger", ages, timelines; no "builds/boosts collagen"; no "clinically"; no treatments or
  competitors (Botox, fillers, retinol, brand names); no body areas, body shape or weight.
- **No before/after, no side-by-side skin, no face close-up "results".** No bodybuilding or "huge" physique (bible Hard NO).
- Never a strength, percentage or size (the label render has none; never add one). No tablets, capsules, droppers, needles, vials.
- No "Are you/Do you…?" questions, no first person, no named competitors.
- Images: the name big, never "by Everlife". Proof wording exact; disclaimer verbatim (the finisher adds both).
